candidates.claim: The first effective entry of CORP_IN, bound to the corp interface, permits 192.168.30.45 to reach engineering workstation 10.10.10.40 on tcp/3389, giving corporate IT a direct connection into the OT side.
candidates.remediation: Remove the CORP_IN entry at fw-01:60 and route this access through the jump host 10.10.20.30 under approved service A4.

candidates.claim: Corporate traffic to engineering workstation 10.10.10.40 on tcp/3389 is permitted by fw-01:60, but the only approved path to that workstation is the jump host 10.10.20.30 (A4), so this cross-zone flow bypasses DMZ mediation.
candidates.remediation: Remove the CORP_IN entry at fw-01:60 so corporate access to the engineering workstation goes only through the jump host.

candidates.claim: EDGE_IN on rtr-01 permits any source on tcp/443 to 203.0.113.2, the outside address of fw-01, and fw-01 has its HTTP/ASDM server enabled, so HTTPS management of fw-01 is reachable from outside the mgmt interface, contrary to the management policy.
candidates.remediation: Remove or restrict the tcp/443 permit at rtr-01:68 so that fw-01 HTTPS/ASDM management is reachable only from MGMT 10.10.99.0/24 on the mgmt interface.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 holds a second default route 0.0.0.0/0 with next hop 10.10.99.1, the MGMT firewall interface, alongside the default route to the ISP, which creates a route from the MGMT zone toward OUTSIDE outside the approved services.
candidates.remediation: Remove the default route via 10.10.99.1 at rtr-01:55 and keep only the default route via 198.51.100.1 at rtr-01:54.

candidates.claim: The baseline delta shows that the CORP_IN access-list entry at fw-01:60 was added and is not in the approved baseline, so it must be reconciled.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile fw-01:60 against the approved baseline and revert it unless an approved exception exists.
